steps.body: Shape categories nest like a **family tree**, and attributes are **inherited**: if EVERY member of a category has an attribute, then every member of any subcategory inside it has that attribute too. Every rectangle has 4 right angles; a square is a kind of rectangle; so every square has 4 right angles — no measuring needed.

widget.prompt: Every parallelogram has two pairs of parallel sides. Rectangles are parallelograms. What can you conclude?

choices.label: Every rectangle has two pairs of parallel sides
choices.feedback: Right — rectangles sit inside the parallelogram category, so they inherit its attribute.
choices.evidenceText: The property follows the arrow from parallelogram to rectangle.

choices.label: Every parallelogram is a rectangle
choices.feedback: That reverses the nesting. Rectangles sit inside parallelograms, not the other way — a tilted parallelogram has no right angles.
choices.evidenceText: The reverse arrow would erase the rectangle's extra right-angle condition.

choices.label: Only some rectangles have parallel sides
choices.feedback: Inheritance is an EVERY, not a some: every member of the subcategory gets the category's attribute.
choices.evidenceText: Every member of the inside family inherits the property; it is not optional.

widget.successFeedback: Right — rectangles sit inside the parallelogram category, so they inherit its attribute.

hints: Attributes ride down into the smaller category.
explanationVariants: Subcategories inherit: all rectangles get the parallel pairs.
Rectangle ⊂ parallelogram, so the attribute carries down.
Every rectangle has 4; squares are rectangles.

widget.prompt: Every rectangle has 4 right angles. A square is a special rectangle. How many right angles must a square have?

choices.feedback: Right — squares inherit all-rectangle attributes, so 4 right angles is guaranteed.
choices.evidenceText: The four-right-angle property travels from rectangle to square.

choices.label: It depends on the square
choices.feedback: It can't depend — every square is a rectangle, and EVERY rectangle has 4 right angles. Inheritance leaves no exceptions.
choices.evidenceText: No square counterexample can exist because square is inside rectangle.

choices.feedback: 2 would break the inherited attribute. Squares are rectangles, so all 4 corners are right angles.
choices.evidenceText: Two right angles conflict with the inherited four-corner structure.

widget.fallbackFeedback: Use the family path, fixed triangle givens, or the required example, counterexample, or blocker evidence.
widget.successFeedback: Right — squares inherit all-rectangle attributes, so 4 right angles is guaranteed.

steps.body: The arrow points **only downward**. What's true of the big category is true of the small one inside it — never the reverse. Every square has 4 equal sides, and squares are rectangles; that does NOT make every rectangle equal-sided. Counterexample: a 5-by-2 rectangle has sides 5, 2, 5, 2 — a fine rectangle, sides not all equal.

explanationVariants: Upward inheritance is the error; 5-by-2 is the counterexample.
Square attributes don't climb the tree.

widget.prompt: "Every square has 4 equal sides. Squares are rectangles. So every rectangle has 4 equal sides." What's wrong with this argument?

choices.label: It runs the wrong way — attributes pass down to subcategories, not up
choices.feedback: Right — a 5-by-2 rectangle has sides 5, 2, 5, 2, so the conclusion is false. Square facts stay with squares.
choices.evidenceText: The proposed argument climbs from square to rectangle, opposite the inheritance arrow.

choices.label: Nothing — the conclusion is correct
choices.feedback: Test it on a 5-by-2 rectangle: sides 5, 2, 5, 2 are not all equal. The argument pushed a square attribute up onto all rectangles.
choices.evidenceText: A 5-by-2 rectangle supplies a visible counterexample to the reversed claim.

choices.label: Squares aren't really rectangles
choices.feedback: Squares ARE rectangles — that premise is fine. The flaw is the direction: what's true of squares needn't be true of all rectangles.
choices.evidenceText: Square membership in rectangle is true; only the direction of inheritance is false.

widget.fallbackFeedback: Use the family path, fixed triangle givens, or the required example, counterexample, or blocker evidence.
widget.successFeedback: Right — a 5-by-2 rectangle has sides 5, 2, 5, 2, so the conclusion is false. Square facts stay with squares.

hints: Which way does the argument push the attribute?
Down is valid; up is not.

widget.prompt: Every rectangle has 4 right angles of 90° each. What do a rectangle's four angles add up to, in degrees?

commonErrors.feedback: 180° is a TRIANGLE's angle sum. A rectangle has four 90° corners: 4 × 90 = 360°.
90° is one corner. Add all four: 4 × 90 = 360°.

explanationVariants: Every square inherits equal sides from rhombuses.
Square ⊂ rhombus carries the attribute down.

widget.prompt: Every rhombus has 4 equal sides. Squares are rhombuses. What MUST be true?

choices.label: Every square has 4 equal sides
choices.feedback: Right — squares inherit the rhombus family's equal sides.
choices.evidenceText: Four equal sides travel down from rhombus to square.

choices.label: Every rhombus is a square
choices.feedback: That reverses the nesting — a tilted rhombus with no right angles is not a square. Squares sit inside rhombuses.
choices.evidenceText: A tilted rhombus blocks the reverse claim.

choices.label: Some squares have unequal sides
choices.feedback: That would contradict inheritance: every square is a rhombus, and EVERY rhombus has equal sides.
choices.evidenceText: Unequal square sides contradict the inherited rhombus condition.

widget.fallbackFeedback: Use the family path, fixed triangle givens, or the required example, counterexample, or blocker evidence.
widget.successFeedback: Right — squares inherit the rhombus family's equal sides.

hints: Follow the chain: square → rectangle → parallelogram.
The attribute starts at the top of the chain.
It rides down through both levels to the square.
explanationVariants: The attribute descends two levels: parallelogram → rectangle → square.
Square ⊂ rectangle ⊂ parallelogram, so squares inherit parallel pairs from the top.

widget.prompt: Every parallelogram has two pairs of parallel sides. Every rectangle is a parallelogram. Every square is a rectangle. What MUST be true of every square?

choices.label: It has two pairs of parallel sides — inherited down two levels
choices.feedback: Right — the attribute rides from parallelograms through rectangles down to squares.
choices.evidenceText: The property crosses both arrows to reach every square.

choices.label: It is the only shape with parallel sides
choices.feedback: Inheritance shares attributes downward; it never makes the smallest category the ONLY holder. All parallelograms have them.
choices.evidenceText: The broader parallelogram and rectangle nodes keep the same property too.

choices.label: Every parallelogram is a square
choices.feedback: That reverses the chain twice. Squares sit at the bottom of this branch, inside rectangles, inside parallelograms.
choices.evidenceText: Reversing both arrows would erase the extra conditions at each level.

widget.fallbackFeedback: Use the family path, fixed triangle givens, or the required example, counterexample, or blocker evidence.
widget.successFeedback: Right — the attribute rides from parallelograms through rectangles down to squares.

takeaways: If every member of a category has an attribute, every subcategory member inherits it.
The arrow points down only — subcategory attributes don't climb (5-by-2 rectangle!).
Chains work: attributes ride down through several levels at once.

concept.body: Quick rewind. **Inside means inherits.** If squares sit inside the rectangle category, then anything true of ALL rectangles is automatically true of every square. Ask two questions: which group sits inside which, and what does everyone in the big group have?

explanationVariants: Squares are rectangles, so they inherit the 4 right angles.
Inside means inherits: 4 right angles, guaranteed.

widget.prompt: Every rectangle has 4 right angles, and squares are rectangles. So every square has…

choices.label: 4 right angles
choices.feedback: Right — inherited from the rectangle category.
choices.evidenceText: The four right angles travel down the family arrow.

choices.label: no right angles
choices.feedback: Squares are rectangles, and every rectangle has 4 right angles — inheritance guarantees them.
choices.evidenceText: Zero right angles conflicts with rectangle membership.

choices.label: right angles only sometimes
choices.feedback: Inheritance has no sometimes: every square is a rectangle, so every square gets all 4.
choices.evidenceText: Inheritance applies to every square, not only some.

widget.successFeedback: Right — inherited from the rectangle category.
